title: What a saga! Love this guy! #danielradcliffe #broadway #westend #harr...
transcript: Daniel Radcliffe's career as a stage actor might be even more interesting than you realize so in today's very special episode of Overthinking Theatre Throwback I'm gonna do a retrospective on the 9 stage roles he's played over the years and analyze the arc of it all the triumphs and pitfalls he's encountered along the way and the fascinating double edged sword of always challenging himself in the way that he does. My qualifications are that I have seen 8 out of these nine 9 performances live the only one I didn't see live was Equus which I have seen an archival pro-shot of so I like to joke that I am the foremost scholar of Daniel Radcliffe's stage career and it has been an endless source of fascination for me. his first stage performance came in 2007 at 18 years old while the Harry Potter movies we're still coming out and it was a massive undertaking this was a revival of *Peter* Shaffer's Equus in which he famously appeared nude but even beyond that it's an incredibly intense show and role and my impression from the pro-shot is that he captured that intensity pretty effectively although maybe in a bit of a one-note way where it maybe wasn't the mature nuance display of acting that we would see from him later on of course he switched tack entirely in his second stage outing as J Peirpont Finch in the Pulitzer Prize winning musical how to succeed in business without really trying he literally learned how to sing and dance for this role and the singing is pretty impressive but the dancing is kind of on a crazy level like go back and watch his Tony performance and it's like wow, he's really doing that! after Equus and how to succeed he did a string of plays that didn't get quite as much media attention but in that time he was continuing to stretch himself and find his strengths he starred in a revival of Martin Mcdonagh's dark comedy The Cripple of Innishmaan where he attempted a quite questionable Irish accent but he still turned in a solid, charming performance nonetheless in 2016 he did a play called Privacy Off-Broadway which was kind of like an interactive PSA about digital privacy online the audience had their phones out it was actually quite bad but he wasn't the problem with it he was kind of just doing his usual thing. he did two productions of the Old Vic in London in 2017, Rosencrantz and gildenstern are dead and in 2020 Endgame those were by Tom Stoppard and Samuel Beckett respectively two playwrights who are notoriously challenging in their intellectual density in between he did a much lighter project a play called The Lifespan of a fact on on Broadway where he played a comically pedantic fact-checker for an article the play was pretty lightweight but the role was kind of a layup for him it was very solidly in his wheel house and I think it's around this time that Radcliffe started to realize that while he's a perfectly capable dramatic actor comedy might be more his forte. both on stage and on screen I think he's become a really respectable comedic actor in his own right but just as he's starting to get comfortable in that sphere he does what he always does and challenges himself yet again doing another musical but one that couldn't be more different from how to succeed not only a much trickier score by Sondheim but under Maria Friedman's direction back in the world of grounded drama I still maintain that his singing in this was a little shaky even compared to the admittedly simpler melodies in how to succeed but acting-wise he really knocked it out of the park and even vocally he still pulled it off and for Merrily we roll along he finally got some long overdue recognition from the Tony Awards he'd never even been nominated but here he won! as much as I admire him I do think there's a reason he was never nominated before by taking on so many challenges he earned a lot of respect but was also constantly putting himself in this position of just barely pulling everything off. he became the classic Jack of all trades but master of none and I think where this was most visible was with his co-stars who were visibly more experienced in whatever genre he was working in. Outshined by John Larroquette in how to succeed by Sarah Greene in The Cripple of Inishmaan by Joshua Mcguire in Rosencrantz and gildenstern by Alan Cumming in Endgame And yeah in my opinion even Jonathan Groff and Lindsay Mendez in merrily which is why it's particularly funny to me that he's now doing Every Brilliant Thing a one man show! but even here I thought his performance suffered a little bit from the emphasis they placed on the interactive gimmick so ironically, in a symbolic sense you could say that even the audience volunteers are kind of outshining him (though not literally) despite the double edge sword here I am still excited to see him take on these new challenges I've been saying for years that I'd love to see him tackle Shakespeare and I asked him about it at the stage door once and he said he was way too intimidated by it he said “you're gonna have to wait a long time for that one mate!” in any case I love that he has embraced theatre to an extent that few film stars ever do and even when they do it's usually because they got their start in theatre so Daniel Radcliffe is something of a unicorn and after 9 roles over the course of 12 different runs I think it's fair to say that he is an accomplished stage actor in his own right.
